Description: The Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) was established in 2011. It provides a cost-effective, risk-based approach for the adoption and use of cloud services by the U.S. federal government. FedRAMP empowers federal agencies to use modern cloud technologies, with an emphasis on the security and protection of federal information. This framework covers the controls for FedRAMP Moderate Revision 5 based on NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(1) Automated System Account Management
Requirements.Description: The organization employs automated mechanisms to support the management of information system accounts.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(4) Automated Audit Actions
Requirements.Description: The information system automatically audits account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions, and notifies [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].

Requirements.Name: AC-2(12)(a)
Requirements.Description: The organization: a. Monitors information system accounts for [Assignment: organization-defined atypical use].

Requirements.Name: AC-2(d)
Requirements.Description: Notify account managers of user account changes including terminations, transfers, or role changes.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(f)
Requirements.Description: The organization: f. Creates, enables, modifies, disables, and removes information system accounts in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined procedures or conditions].

Requirements.Name: AC-2(g)
Requirements.Description: The organization: g. Monitors the use of information system accounts.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(j)
Requirements.Description: The organization: j. Reviews accounts for compliance with account management requirements [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

Requirements.Name: AC-2(2) Temporary and Emergency Account Management
Requirements.Description: Automatically disable temporary and emergency accounts after a defined time period.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(3) Disable Accounts
Requirements.Description: Automatically disable inactive accounts after 90 days for user accounts.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(3)(c) Monitor Shared/Group Account Usage
Requirements.Description: Monitor the use of shared/group accounts.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(7)(a) Account Credential Reissuance
Requirements.Description: Establish and follow a process for reissuing shared/group account credentials when individuals are removed from the group.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(7)(c) Password Hashing
Requirements.Description: Store passwords using hashing with a salt.

Requirements.Name: Access Enforcement (AC-3)
Requirements.Description: The information system enforces approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.

Requirements.Name: Information Flow Enforcement (AC-4)
Requirements.Description: The information system enforces approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between interconnected systems based on organization-defined information flow control policies.

Requirements.Name: AC-4(21) Information Flow Enforcement - Automatic Mechanism
Requirements.Description: Employ automated mechanisms to assist in information flow enforcement.

Requirements.Name: AC-5(c)
Requirements.Description: The organization: c. Defines information system access authorizations to support separation of duties.

Requirements.Name: AC-6(10) Prohibit Non-Privileged Users From Executing Privileged Functions
Requirements.Description: The information system prevents non-privileged users from executing privileged functions to include disabling, circumventing, or altering implemented security safeguards/countermeasures.

Requirements.Name: Least Privilege (AC-6)
Requirements.Description: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) which are necessary to accomplish assigned tasks in accordance with organizational missions and business functions.

Requirements.Name: AC-6(2) Non-Privileged Access For Nonsecurity Functions
Requirements.Description: Require that users of system accounts use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions.

Requirements.Name: AC-6(5) Privileged Accounts
Requirements.Description: Restrict privileged accounts on the system to personnel or roles with security administration responsibilities.

Requirements.Name: AC-6(7) Review of User Privileges
Requirements.Description: Review privileges prior to granting privileged access.

Requirements.Name: AC-6(9) Log Use Of Privileged Functions
Requirements.Description: Log the execution of privileged functions.

Requirements.Name: AC-17(1) Automated Monitoring/Control
Requirements.Description: The information system monitors and controls remote access methods.

Requirements.Name: AC-17(2) Protection Of Confidentiality/Integrity Using Encryption
Requirements.Description: The information system implements cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality and integrity of remote access sessions.

Requirements.Name: AC-21(b)
Requirements.Description: The organization: b. Employs [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms or manual processes] to assist users in making information sharing/collaboration decisions.

Requirements.Name: AU-2(a)(d)
Requirements.Description: The organization: a. Determines that the information system is capable of auditing the following events: Successful and unsuccessful account logon events, account management events, object access, policy change, privilege functions, process tracking, and system events. For Web applications: all administrator activity, authentication checks, authorization checks, data deletions, data access, data changes, and permission changes. d. Determines that the following events are to be audited within the information system: [organization-defined subset of the auditable events defined in AU-2 a to be audited continually for each identified event].

Requirements.Name: Content of Audit Records (AU-3)
Requirements.Description: The information system generates audit records containing information that establishes what type of event occurred, when the event occurred, where the event occurred, the source of the event, the outcome of the event, and the identity of any individuals or subjects associated with the event.

Requirements.Name: AU-6(1)(3)
Requirements.Description: (1) The organization employs automated mechanisms to integrate audit review, analysis, and reporting processes to support organizational processes for investigation and response to suspicious activities. (3) The organization analyzes and correlates audit records across different repositories to gain organization-wide situational awareness.

Requirements.Name: AU-7(1) Automatic Processing
Requirements.Description: The information system provides the capability to process audit records for events of interest based on [Assignment: organization-defined audit fields within audit records].

Requirements.Name: AU-9(2) Store on Separate Physical Systems or Components
Requirements.Description: Store audit records [FedRAMP Assignment: at least weekly] in a repository that is part of a physically different system or system component than the system or component being audited.

Requirements.Name: Protection of Audit Information (AU-9)
Requirements.Description: The information system protects audit information and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.

Requirements.Name: AU-6(1) Process Integration
Requirements.Description: Integrate audit review, analysis, and reporting processes to support organizational processes for investigation and response to suspicious activities.

Requirements.Name: Audit Record Retention (AU-11)
Requirements.Description: The organization retains audit records for at least 90 days to provide support for after-the-fact investigations of security incidents and to meet regulatory and organizational information retention requirements.

Requirements.Name: AU-12(a)(c)
Requirements.Description: The information system: a. Provides audit record generation capability for the auditable events defined in AU-2 a. at all information system and network components where audit capability is deployed/available c. Generates audit records for the events defined in AU-2 d. with the content defined in AU-3.

Requirements.Name: CA-7(a)(b)
Requirements.Description: The organization develops a continuous monitoring strategy and implements a continuous monitoring program that includes: a. Establishment of [Assignment: organization-defined metrics] to be monitored; b. Establishment of [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] for monitoring and [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] for assessments supporting such monitoring.

Requirements.Name: Baseline Configuration (CM-2)
Requirements.Description: The organization develops, documents, and maintains under configuration control, a current baseline configuration of the information system.

Requirements.Name: Configuration Settings (CM-6)
Requirements.Description: Establish and document configuration settings for components employed within the system that reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements.

Requirements.Name: CM-7(a)
Requirements.Description: The organization: a. Configures the information system to provide only essential capabilities.

Requirements.Name: CM-8(1)
Requirements.Description: The organization updates the inventory of information system components as an integral part of component installations, removals, and information system updates.

Requirements.Name: CM-8(3)(a)
Requirements.Description: The organization: a. Employs automated mechanisms continuously, using automated mechanisms with a maximum five-minute delay in detection, to detect the presence of unauthorized hardware, software, and firmware components within the information system

Requirements.Name: CP-9(b))
Requirements.Description: The organization: b. Conducts backups of system-level information contained in the information system (daily incremental; weekly full).

Requirements.Name: Information System Recovery And Reconstitution (CP-10)
Requirements.Description: The organization provides for the recovery and reconstitution of the information system to a known state after a disruption, compromise, or failure.

Requirements.Name: IA-2(2) Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | Multi-factor Authentication to Non-privileged Accounts​​​​​​​
Requirements.Description: Implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts.

Attributes.SubSection: IA-2(2) Multi-factor Authentication to Non-privileged Accounts​​​​​​​

Requirements.Name: IA-2(1): Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | Multi-factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts
Requirements.Description: Implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts.

Attributes.SubSection: IA-2(1) Multi-factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts

Requirements.Name: Identification and Authentication (Organizational users) (IA-2)
Requirements.Description: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.

Requirements.Name: IA-5(1)(a)(d)(e)
Requirements.Description: The information system, for password-based authentication: a. Enforces minimum password complexity of [Assignment: organization-defined requirements for case sensitivity, number of characters, mix of upper-case letters, lower-case letters, numbers, and special characters, including minimum requirements for each type]; d. Enforces password minimum and maximum lifetime restrictions of [Assignment: organization- defined numbers for lifetime minimum, lifetime maximum]; e. Prohibits password reuse for 24 generations

Requirements.Name: IA-5(1)(b) Minimum Password Length
Requirements.Description: Enforce at least the following number of characters for passwords: 12 characters for privileged accounts and 8 characters for non-privileged accounts.

Requirements.Name: IA-5(4) Automated Support For Password Strength Determination
Requirements.Description: The organization employs automated tools to determine if password authenticators are sufficiently strong to satisfy [Assignment: organization-defined requirements].

Requirements.Name: IA-5(7) No Embedded Unencrypted Static Authenticators
Requirements.Description: The organization ensures that unencrypted static authenticators are not embedded in applications or access scripts or stored on function keys.

Requirements.Name: IR-4(1) Automated Incident Handling Processes
Requirements.Description: Employ automated mechanisms to support the incident handling process.

Requirements.Name: IR-6(1) Automated Reporting
Requirements.Description: The organization employs automated mechanisms to assist in the reporting of security incidents.

Requirements.Name: IR-7(1) Automation Support For Availability Of Information / Support
Requirements.Description: The organization employs automated mechanisms to increase the availability of incident response-related information and support.

Requirements.Name: Vulnerability Scanning (RA-5)
Requirements.Description: Scan for system vulnerabilities. Share vulnerability information and security controls that eliminate vulnerabilities.

Requirements.Name: RA-5(2) Update Vulnerabilities to Be Scanned
Requirements.Description: Update the system vulnerability monitoring tools before conducting scans and when new vulnerabilities are identified.

Requirements.Name: SA-3(a)
Requirements.Description: The organization: a. Manages the information system using [Assignment: organization-defined system development life cycle] that incorporates information security considerations.

Requirements.Name: Developer Configuration Management (SA-10)
Requirements.Description: The organization requires the developer of the information system, system component, or information system service to: a. Perform configuration management during system, component, or service [Selection (one or more): design; development; implementation; operation]; b. Document, manage, and control the integrity of changes to [Assignment: organization-defined configuration items under configuration management]; c. Implement only organization-approved changes to the system, component, or service; d. Document approved changes to the system, component, or service and the potential security impacts of such changes; and e. Track security flaws and flaw resolution within the system, component, or service and report findings to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel].

Requirements.Name: Application Partitioning (SC-2)
Requirements.Description: The information system separates user functionality (including user interface services) from information system management functionality.

Requirements.Name: Information In Shared Resources (SC-4)
Requirements.Description: The information system prevents unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.

Requirements.Name: Denial Of Service Protection (SC-5)
Requirements.Description: The information system protects against or limits the effects of the following types of denial of service attacks: [Assignment: organization-defined types of denial of service attacks or references to sources for such information] by employing [Assignment: organization-defined security safeguards].

Requirements.Name: SC-7(3) Access Points
Requirements.Description: The organization limits the number of external network connections to the information system.

Requirements.Name: Boundary Protection (SC-7)
Requirements.Description: The information system: a. Monitors and controls communications at the external boundary of the system and at key internal boundaries within the system; b. Implements subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are [Selection: physically; logically] separated from internal organizational networks; and c. Connects to external networks or information systems only through managed interfaces consisting of boundary protection devices arranged in accordance with an organizational security architecture.

Requirements.Name: SC-8(1) Cryptographic Or Alternate Physical Protection
Requirements.Description: The information system implements cryptographic mechanisms to [Selection (one or more): prevent unauthorized disclosure of information; detect changes to information] during transmission unless otherwise protected by [Assignment: organization-defined alternative physical safeguards].

Requirements.Name: Transmission Integrity (SC-8)
Requirements.Description: The information system protects the confidentiality AND integrity of transmitted information.

Requirements.Name: Cryptographic Key Establishment And Management (SC-12)
Requirements.Description: The organization establishes and manages cryptographic keys for required cryptography employed within the information system in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined requirements for key generation, distribution, storage, access, and destruction].

Requirements.Name: Use of Cryptography (SC-13)
Requirements.Description: The information system implements FIPS-validated or NSA-approved cryptography in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards.

Requirements.Name: Session Authenticity (SC-23)
Requirements.Description: The information system protects the authenticity of communications sessions.

Requirements.Name: Protection of Information at Rest (SC-28)
Requirements.Description: The information system protects the confidentiality AND integrity of [Assignment: organization-defined information at rest].

Requirements.Name: SC-28(1) Cryptographic Protection
Requirements.Description: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of information at rest.

Requirements.Name: Automated Flaw Remediation Status (SI-2(2))
Requirements.Description: The organization employs automated mechanisms at least monthly to determine the state of information system components with regard to flaw remediation.

Requirements.Name: SI-3(a) Malicious Code Protection
Requirements.Description: Implement malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code.

Requirements.Name: SI-3(b) Update Malicious Code Protection
Requirements.Description: Update malicious code protection mechanisms whenever new releases are available.

Requirements.Name: SI-4(5) System-Generated Alerts - Unauthorized Software
Requirements.Description: Employ automated mechanisms to detect the presence of unauthorized software on organizational information systems and notify designated organizational officials.

Requirements.Name: SI-6(a) Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity - Verify Integrity
Requirements.Description: Verify software, firmware, and information integrity weekly using tools, techniques, and/or mechanisms with a verifiable audit trail.

Requirements.Name: SI-8(a) Spam Protection
Requirements.Description: Employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and act on unsolicited messages.

Requirements.Name: SI-8(2) Automatic Updates
Requirements.Description: Update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available.

Requirements.Name: SI-16 Malicious Code Incident Analysis and Handling
Requirements.Description: Develop, document, and maintain a capability designed to analyze and handle malicious code incidents.

Requirements.Name: SI-4(1) System-Wide Intrusion Detection System
Requirements.Description: The organization connects and configures individual intrusion detection tools into an information system-wide intrusion detection system.

Requirements.Name: SI-4(16) Correlate Monitoring Information
Requirements.Description: The organization correlates information from monitoring tools employed throughout the information system.

Requirements.Name: SI-4(2) Automated Tools For Real-Time Analysis
Requirements.Description: The organization employs automated tools to support near real-time analysis of events.

Requirements.Name: SI-4(4) Inbound and Outbound Communications Traffic
Requirements.Description: The information system monitors inbound and outbound communications traffic continuously for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions.

Requirements.Name: SI-4(5) System-Generated Alerts
Requirements.Description: The information system alerts organization-defined personnel or roles when the following indications of compromise or potential compromise occur: [Assignment: organization-defined compromise indicators].

Requirements.Name: SI-4(a)(b)(c)
Requirements.Description: The organization: a. Monitors the information system to detect: 1. Attacks and indicators of potential attacks in accordance with [Assignment: organization- defined monitoring objectives]; and 2. Unauthorized local, network, and remote connections; b. Identifies unauthorized use of the information system through [Assignment: organization- defined techniques and methods]; c. Deploys monitoring devices: i. strategically within the information system to collect organization-determined essential information; and (ii) at ad hoc locations within the system to track specific types of transactions of interest to the organization.

Requirements.Name: SI-7(1) Integrity Checks
Requirements.Description: The information system performs an integrity check of security relevant events at least monthly.

Requirements.Name: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity (SI-7)
Requirements.Description: The organization employs integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to [Assignment: organization-defined software, firmware, and information].

Requirements.Name: Information Handling and Retention (SI-12)
Requirements.Description: The organization handles and retains information within the information system and information output from the system in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and operational requirements.

Requirements.Name: AC-11(a) Session Lock
Requirements.Description: Employ session lock with pattern-hiding displays to prevent access/viewing of data after a period of inactivity.

Requirements.Name: AC-11(b) Session Lock Continuation
Requirements.Description: Retain the session lock until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures.

Requirements.Name: AC-11(1) Pattern-Hiding Displays
Requirements.Description: Allow users to initiate a session lock with pattern-hiding displays.

Requirements.Name: AC-2(9) Termination of Access
Requirements.Description: Notify account managers when accounts are no longer required, when users are terminated or transferred, or when system usage or need-to-know changes.

Requirements.Name: SR-03(b) Software Repair Strategy
Requirements.Description: Employ a strategy for software repairs that includes near-term, mid-term, and long-term goals.
